headline: High: TREK’s MCP/browser surface and secret-bearing workspace create dangerous default pathways for leakage and cascading errors when paired with EMQX’s broad network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK exposes MCP and browser-driven inputs, so attacker-controlled content can reach its tool-use path; EMQX has broad network egress and HTTP API output but no documented parser hardening. The pair lacks a shared channel in the profiles, so this is not high, but TREK’s collaborative real-time surface makes instruction hijacking plausible.
conditions: IF TREK ingests browser or MCP content as instructions without provenance checks, prompt injection is possible.
IF EMQX output is copied into TREK’s collaborative session, malicious instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Disable MCP tools for untrusted sessions.
Require provenance labels on browser-sourced text.
Strip instructions from imported web content.
Use a manual review step before TREK acts on EMQX-derived text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and files under ./data and ./uploads, while EMQX has broad network egress. That combination creates a direct exfiltration path if TREK content is surfaced to EMQX or if EMQX forwards context externally. The profiles do not show isolation between them, so uncertainty escalates.
conditions: IF TREK data is passed into EMQX outputs or logs, sensitive travel and secret data can leak.
IF EMQX is allowed to transmit received content off-host, secrets in TREK can be exfiltrated.
mitigations: Do not route TREK secrets into EMQX.
Redact API keys and MFA secrets before any handoff.
Restrict EMQX egress to approved destinations only.
Separate TREK data files from any EMQX-accessible workspace.
Rotate exposed secrets immediately if sharing already occurred.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: TREK supports real-time collaborative sessions and multiple instances, and it writes to local files like ./data/travel.db and ./uploads/. EMQX has HTTP API egress but no write surface is documented, so direct write-write conflict is not proven. Still, shared mutable resources in TREK make coordination failures plausible if both agents touch the same workspace.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same TREK database or uploads directory, concurrent modification conflicts can occur.
IF EMQX is extended to write files or state in the same workspace, lockless races become likely.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Disable concurrent edits to ./data/travel.db.
Use file locks for uploads and database updates.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is described as a real-time collaborative travel planner with AI built in, so it may treat upstream text as actionable planning input; EMQX can emit networked outputs broadly. If EMQX-generated content is fed into TREK without verification, TREK could propagate incorrect plans or actions. The profiles do not show a verification gate, so the safer higher severity applies.
conditions: IF TREK consumes EMQX output as authoritative planning input, errors can cascade into downstream actions.
IF EMQX emits malformed or adversarial text and TREK auto-acts on it, the cascade persists.
mitigations: Require human review before TREK acts on EMQX output.
Add schema validation to all EMQX-to-TREK messages.
Mark EMQX content as untrusted by default.
Log and diff imported recommendations before execution.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles reservations, documents, photos, country visit history, and secrets, while EMQX touches IoT data and has broad egress. The profiles do not state residency or certification mismatches, so compliance risk is inferred from data-class handling and logging surfaces rather than a proven violation. Uncertainty keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF TREK stores personal travel records in logs or uploads that EMQX can access, retention and residency controls may diverge.
IF EU-origin travel data is forwarded through EMQX to external services, a policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Review retention settings for ./data/logs/trek.log.
Keep travel documents out of EMQX-accessible paths.
Document data residency for any EMQX egress destination.
Purge logs containing reservations or identifiers.
requires-engineering: align retention and subject-rights workflows.
